newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to meet chief aide at country residence.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet chief aide at country residence.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, will meet chief aide Anatoly Chubais and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov at his country residence outside Moscow on Friday, a Kremlin spokesman said.

Since his release from hospital on January 20, Yeltsin has made three appearances at the Kremlin to counter opposition suggestions that he is unfit to rule. But the spokesman said Friday's talks, two days before a visit by French President Jacques Chirac, would be held at his Gorky-9 residence.

Official television film showed Yeltsin smiling broadly but clearly moving with some difficulty at a meeting on Thursday in the Kremlin with Constitutional Court head Vladimir Tumanov. His face was rather drawn and he had clearly aged since heart bypass surgery on November 5.
At one point he appeared to be expressing a desire to return quickly to a more active life, but Tumanov could be heard telling him: "Don't hurry."

Sunday's meeting with Chirac will mark the first direct encounter with a Western leader since his release from hospital and an important step for the president as he attempts to reassert his authority at home and on the world stage.

Yeltsin has been advised by doctors not to rush his return to work, but the president is under strong pressure to show he is capable of exercising presidential powers. The communists, strongest party in the State Duma parliament, and presidential rival Alexander Lebed have called on him to step down.
Opponents portray Chubais, architect of Russia's huge privatisation campaign, as a dark force in the country's politics, using Yeltsin's absences to extend his own powers.
